title: Perl
subtitle: The text-processing language that holds much of the Unix world together, from a first script to regular expressions, references, objects, tests and a complete log analyser.
description: Perl is a general-purpose scripting language created by Larry Wall in 1987 to make report-writing and text-wrangling on Unix easy. It became the glue of the early web and of system administration, and it is still installed on almost every Linux and macOS machine. Today you meet it in system scripts and build tools, in bioinformatics pipelines, in long-lived web applications, and anywhere people need to tear through text quickly. Its regular expressions were so good that most other languages copied them. Perl 5 is the language this course teaches; its sibling Raku (once called Perl 6) is a separate language.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It begins with Perl's history and your first scripts, works through scalars, arrays and hashes and the idea of context, subroutines, references and nested data, regular expressions in depth, and files and text, and ends with modules and CPAN, object-oriented Perl, testing with Test::More, and a complete log analyser.

To run the code you need a `perl` command. On Linux and macOS it is almost certainly installed already (`perl -v` tells you which version); [perl.org/get.html](https://www.perl.org/get.html) lists the official ways to get a newer one, including Strawberry Perl for Windows and perlbrew for managing several versions. There is no official online playground. Every complete program in these lessons was run with Perl 5.34 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed; each program also runs unchanged on newer releases, and the lessons point out what Perl 5.36 and later add. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Run your first scripts with strict and warnings on, then learn Perl's three kinds of variable and their sigils, the idea of context, control flow, and subroutines.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Build nested data with references, master regular expressions, Perl's great strength, and read, transform and write files while handling errors properly.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Organise code into modules, use CPAN, write object-oriented Perl, test it with Test::More, and build a complete log analyser the way working Perl programmers do.
